subject: Post-call: FinCorp eval scope & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fincorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-29T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: FinCorp eval scope & next steps

Thanks Alex — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we start the evals.

Call recap (your goals):
- Reduce manual routing errors in claims triage; prioritize minimizing hallucinations on factual fields (claim type, policy ID).
- Maintain sub-200ms median token latency for live assistant flows.
- Keep per-token cost predictable; want a comparison across a few model/quantization options.

Initial evaluation scope (what Redwood will run once we have inputs):
- Run comparative eval across 3 model variants (small/medium/quantized) on your sample dataset.
- Metrics: exact-match on structured fields, token-level latency, hallucination rate (measured via entailment model), and human-graded quality on a 1-5 scale for 200-sample subset.
- Deliverables: per-model metrics, sample prompts that failed, and a short ops runbook with recommended batching/kv-cache profiles.

What we need from FinCorp:
1) A sample dataset (CSV) with columns: id, prompt, reference_response, category (optional). 10k rows preferred but we can start with 1k for a quick benchmark.
2) A short scoring rubric (how you want automated vs. human scoring applied).
3) Any PII/data restrictions or redaction requirements.

Attachments I'm including as examples: example_prompt_set.csv (format template) and eval_results_template.xlsx (results template).

Proposed timeline:
- You share dataset + rubric by EOD 2026-10-01.
- Redwood spins up evals and returns initial results within 7 business days after receipt.

Next step: can you confirm dataset availability and whether the 10k target is realistic? Also flag any compliance constraints (PII, residency).

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: example_prompt_set.csv (CSV, sample template)]
[Attachment: eval_results_template.xlsx (Excel, results template)]

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fincorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@fincorp.com>, procurement@fincorp.com, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-29T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinCorp eval scope & next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap. A few quick answers and questions: 

- Dataset: We can provide ~10k anonymized rows for the initial run. The fields you listed look good; we'll include a column that marks high-priority samples for human review.
- PII/residency: Data will be anonymized but may include tokenized policy IDs. We need the evaluation to run within the US region only. Can Redwood confirm data residency and that logs won't be retained beyond the eval window?
- SOC2/compliance: Our procurement/security team will need SOC2 evidence. Looping in Samantha (cc'd) from procurement for the contractual/security checklist.

One ask: can you confirm which model families you recommend for an apples-to-apples cost vs. quality comparison? Also confirm the upload mechanism — will a presigned S3 link work?

I'll aim to get the dataset to you by EOD 2026-10-01.

— Alex
Alex Johnson | Head of AI Prod
FinCorp Bank
[External: procurement@fincorp.com]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fincorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@fincorp.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinCorp eval scope & next steps

Great — thanks for the quick turnaround, Alex. Answers and next steps below.

1) Residency & logs: We can run the evals in the US region and provide temporary presigned S3 upload links for secure ingest. Logs related to the eval will be retained only for the duration of the project and can be purged on request; we'll include that in the eval runbook. I've attached a short SOC2 summary for procurement review (SOC2_summary.pdf).

2) Model recommendations (starting point for the comparison):
- redwood/rosetta-8b-int8 (best cost/quality balance for retrieval-heavy prompts)
- redwood/rosetta-4b-q4 (low-cost option with quantized weights)
- open/llama3-7b (baseline open model for parity checks)

We'll run each model with the same prompt set and measure: exact-match on structured outputs, token latency distribution, BLEU/ROUGE for free-text fields, and a factuality/hallucination signal using our entailment scorer. For human review we'll sample 200 items across categories and use your rubric.

3) Dataset format + rubric (please follow this CSV schema):
- id
- prompt
- reference_response (exact expected output for structured fields)
- category
- priority_flag (high/normal)

Scoring criteria (automated):
- Structured fields: exact-match rate (%)
- Free text: BLEU/ROUGE and normalized edit distance
- Hallucination: % of responses with factual contradictions per entailment model
- Latency: median token latency and 95th percentile

We'll populate the attached eval_results_template.xlsx with per-model metrics and example failure cases.

4) Ops / runbook: We'll include recommended batching settings, kv-cache configuration, and a suggested quantization profile for Dedicated deployments if you want to move to a reserved capacity later.

Next steps:
- Please upload the anonymized CSV to the presigned S3 link we'll share (I'll trigger it when you confirm).
- If the dataset is ~10k, we'll run the full comparison and return results within 7 business days. If you want a quicker smoke test, send a 1k sample and we'll do a 48-hour turnaround.

Proposed sync: 30m technical handoff on 2026-10-05 11:00 AM ET to review dataset mapping and rubric — does that work?

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOC2_summary.pdf]
[Attachment: example_prompt_set.csv]
[Attachment: eval_results_template.xlsx]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.j@fincorp.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@fincorp.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinCorp eval scope & next steps

Looping in a couple internal ops notes so we can move fast once the dataset hits. Alex — thanks for confirming the 10k target and US-only requirement. Two quick items: 

1) Upload: We'll generate a presigned S3 upload link (one-time) and send it to Samantha + Alex. Please use that link to upload the CSV; we'll validate schema and let you know of any mismatches within 24 hours. Link will expire in 7 days.

2) Access & retention: We will run the eval inside our US region and tag the job with your account id. Data will be kept only for the eval window and can be purged on completion; we'll record retention in the runbook and include a purge request form.

3) Timeline / owner: Marissa will own the technical run and deliver the report; I'll coordinate SOC2 evidence and procurement questions. Dev, can you pre-check the eval harness for the three model variants Marissa listed and flag any infra constraints?

Alex/Samantha — we'll send the S3 link and SOC2 summary by EOD today. Once you upload, expect a schema check and a short mapping doc back from us within 24 hours.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
